one_liner: Silicon Labs uC/LIB Cortex-M3/4/7 assembly memcpy packaged as RT-Thread's rt_memcpy; beats RT-Thread's C copy, ties Keil memcpy.
what_it_does: Replaces RT-Thread's kernel rt_memcpy(dst, src, count) with a Thumb-2 assembly routine taken from Silicon Labs' uC/LIB (the uC/OS support library) and ported to RT-Thread in December 2020. Three sources (GNU as, IAR, armasm/RVDS) are picked by SConscript per toolchain; the function keeps rt_memcpy's signature and returns dst. It is installed through the RT-Thread package manager (system packages, enhanced kernel services) and only replaces rt_memcpy, not the C library memcpy.
how_it_is_fast: When source and destination share the same offset modulo 4, it copies 1-3 head bytes to reach word alignment and then moves data with LDMIA/STMIA load/store-multiple of ten registers (R3-R12, 40 bytes per pair), unrolled nine times into a 360-byte loop, then single words, halfwords and bytes for the tail. The README credits the load/store-multiple instructions, not assembly as such. RT-Thread's C version (the newlib-derived word loop) moves 16 bytes per iteration with LDR/STR, which explains the 1.43x on aligned 10,000-byte copies; Keil's library memcpy already uses comparable multi-register copies, hence the near tie.
when_to_use: RT-Thread firmware on Cortex-M3, M4 or M7 that does many large (hundreds of bytes and up) rt_memcpy calls between buffers with the same alignment, e.g. DMA or network buffers, when the kernel is built with its own C rt_memcpy.
GCC or IAR builds where you cannot or do not want to route rt_memcpy to the toolchain's memcpy (RT_KLIBC_USING_LIBC_MEMCPY in RT-Thread 5.x, RT_KSERVICE_USING_STDLIB_MEMCPY in 4.1).
Projects that want a small, auditable, Apache-2.0 copy routine with no dependencies and fixed stack use (44 bytes).
when_not_to_use: Keil/ARM Compiler projects that can call the C library memcpy: the only published number puts it at 906 vs 883 ms, about 2.6% (derived from page data), within run-to-run noise of a single undocumented run.

Buffers whose addresses differ by an odd offset: the routine falls back to a byte-at-a-time LDRB/STRB loop (and to LDRH/STRH halfwords for a 2-byte offset) even though Cortex-M3/4/7 can do unaligned word loads, so it will be far slower than an aligned copy there; no misaligned case was measured.
Short copies: every call checks three arguments and saves 11 registers (STMFD R3-R12 plus PUSH R0) before copying, a fixed cost the 10,000-byte benchmark hides.

Overlapping buffers (no memmove behaviour; overlap is not checked) and cores without Thumb-2 (Cortex-M0/M0+/M23); not usable outside RT-Thread without supplying rt_ubase_t and the build glue yourself.
Projects that need a maintained or versioned dependency: 13 commits, no tags, the package index pins 'latest' = master, last change 2022-06-09.

integration.form: source-drop (RT-Thread online package: one .S file per toolchain plus SConscript)
integration.dependencies: RT-Thread build system (SCons, rtconfig.PLATFORM) and the rt_ubase_t type; the code itself needs nothing
integration.min_toolchain: GNU as with .syntax unified, IAR EWARM, or armasm (Keil MDK armcc; armclang via the same _rvds.S since the 2022-06-09 SConscript change); toolchain versions not documented
integration.platforms: ARMv7-M Thumb-2 cores: Cortex-M3, M4, M7 (README); not M0/M0+/M23
integration.thread_safety: Reentrant: no global state, uses only registers and 44 bytes of the caller's stack (not documented, read from the source)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — drop-in for RT-Thread's rt_memcpy only (same signature and return value); it relies on rt_memcpy being weak (RT-Thread 4.1) or on RT_KLIBC_USING_USER_MEMCPY, which the package Kconfig selects for RT-Thread 5.2.0 and later; it does not replace C library memcpy

gotchas: Relative misalignment is not handled by shifting or unaligned word loads: the maintainer confirms in issue #1 that non-aligned addresses are copied a byte at a time, and the code takes a halfword loop for 2-byte offsets and a byte loop for odd offsets, so 'handles non-word-aligned addresses' means correct, not fast.

The benchmark is one Keil run with no harness in the repo, no MCU, clock, compiler version, optimisation level or buffer alignment; the 1.43x is against RT-Thread's own 16-byte-per-iteration C loop, not against a tuned memcpy. The maintainer's only other data point (issue #1) is an SD-card copy that gained about 500 ms, which he called not significant.

Before the 2022-06-09 SConscript fix, the IAR source was selected only when PLATFORM == 'iar' (RT-Thread uses 'iccarm') and armclang was not listed, so IAR and Keil AC6 builds silently kept the C rt_memcpy; use the current master.
NULL dst or src returns immediately without copying (dst is returned), and the routine saves R3 and R12 although AAPCS does not require it; harmless but adds cycles on every call.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over the Raspberry Pi Pico SDK's pico_mem_ops when the target is an RT-Thread Cortex-M3/M4/M7 rather than an RP2040 Cortex-M0+; FastMemcpy and memcpy_benchmark are x86 SSE/AVX copies and do not apply to microcontrollers. Against the toolchain's own memcpy it offers parity, not a speedup. For Cortex-M copies outside RT-Thread, the catalogue's asm-level-string-and-memory category also lists gamesun/memcpy_fast (Cortex-M4, timed separately for each alignment case) and AJ528/mmemmove (a memmove, so overlap-safe).
verified_claims_summary: One first-party Keil run on an unnamed Cortex-M3/4/7 board copied 10,000 bytes 10,000 times: RT-Thread's C rt_memcpy 1,261 ms, this assembly 883 ms (1.43x, derived from page data), Keil's C library memcpy 906 ms (2.6% slower, derived); that is about 113 MB/s for the assembly (derived from page data). Alignment, MCU, clock and compiler settings are not stated, and no benchmark code is published.
status_note: Abandoned since the 2022-06-09 SConscript fix (13 commits, 12 stars, 2 closed issues, no tags), but it is about 200 lines of Apache-2.0 assembly from Silicon Labs' long-used uC/LIB, small enough to vendor and still listed in the RT-Thread package index with a Kconfig update for RT-Thread 5.2.
